### THREAD 1 — imageSize="md"/"sm" gating for the new gallery

Confirmed facts (verify independently, don't just trust me):
- `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` — `imageSize` prop default was ALREADY `'md'` BEFORE this PR (base worktree, same line: `imageSize = 'md',` at line 124) — this default is NOT new. What IS new is that `'md'` now routes to the new `ZimmProductGallery` instead of the old base `ImageGallery`.
- Base (unmodified, un-overridden) `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view-modal/index.jsx:44` and `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx:466` both explicitly pass `imageSize="sm"` to `<ProductView>` — so they're unaffected by the 'md' routing change. I did NOT check `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view-modal/bundle.jsx` (also imports base ProductView, per my grep) — please check whether IT passes `imageSize` explicitly too, since I left this unverified.
- **The real question**: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (the actual overridden PDP page) renders `<ProductView>` THREE times — once for a standalone product (~line 1055 region), once for the parent of a set/bundle (~line 961), and once PER CHILD PRODUCT inside a `.map()` loop when the PDP shows a set/bundle's child products (~line 987). Read all three call sites in full. Confirm none of the three pass `imageSize` explicitly — if true, ALL THREE (including every individual child product in a multi-item set/bundle) now get the new `ZimmProductGallery` + its "View Gallery" button + full overlay, where before this PR they'd have gotten the old, simpler base `ImageGallery`.
  - Is this tested or clearly intentional? Check `zimmProductGallery`'s and `zimmGalleryOverlay`'s own stories/tests for any "multiple galleries stacked on one page" scenario, and check whether product-detail/index.tsx or product-view/index.tsx's own tests cover a set/bundle child-product gallery render.
  - `ZimmProductGallery` has a `lazy` prop documented (in its own props JSDoc, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductGallery/index.tsx` ~line 55-58): "Defers loading of the first item too, not just the rest. Pass true for set/bundle child contexts where the gallery isn't the primary viewport content — mirrors the base ImageGallery's `lazy` prop this component replaces on the PDP." Trace whether `product-view/index.tsx` actually forwards a `lazy` value down into its `ZimmProductGallery` render call for the 'md' branch, and whether `product-detail/index.tsx`'s per-child-product loop passes anything through `product-view/index.tsx`'s own props that would result in `lazy=true` for child products specifically (e.g. via `isProductPartOfSet`/`isProductPartOfBundle` props already passed at that call site). If nothing wires this through, every child product's gallery hero image would load eager/without the deferral this prop exists for — find the exact `<ZimmProductGallery` JSX call site inside product-view/index.tsx's 'md' branch (search for it — I did not locate its exact line number) and report exactly what it passes for `lazy`/`eager`.

### THREAD 2 — ZimmColourSwatch/ZimmColourSwatchGroup circle variant vs existing square-variant callers

Confirmed entry point: `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:991` — `variant={id === 'color' ? 'circle' : 'square'}` (this is inside product-view's generic variation-attribute swatch renderer — color gets the new 'circle' variant, everything else, e.g. size, keeps 'square'). Also `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:221` passes `variant="circle"` to `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` directly.

Tasks:
- `git diff 4cdfb47f324ce533079345ab7aa1203e4a5af734 HEAD -- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` (122 lines changed) and the equivalent for `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts` (272 lines changed) — read both diffs in FULL. Identify every place the diff touches SQUARE-variant styling (not just adds circle-variant styling) — did adding circle require refactoring shared code that square also depends on? If so, is the square output provably pixel-identical before/after (compare the actual style values, not just "it compiles")?
- Find EVERY current caller of `ZimmColourSwatch`/`ZimmColourSwatchGroup` app-wide (grep beyond just product-view.tsx/product-detail.tsx/zimmGalleryOverlay — check stories, other pages) and confirm which variant each uses and that none silently changed variant or broke.
- Check `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx` and `.../molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` (the .tsx files, 8 and 32 lines changed respectively) for the actual prop-plumbing of the new `variant` value — is `'square'` still the correct default when `variant` is omitted by any caller that predates this PR (i.e. did omitting the prop before this PR behave identically to explicitly passing `variant="square"` now)?

REPORT FORMAT: for every finding — `file:line`, one-sentence defect statement, concrete failure scenario (exact input/state → exact wrong output), confidence (CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE), severity (🔴/🟡/🔵), UNIFORM or ONE-OFF. End with "What I tried to falsify" and "What I could not verify" sections — be specific about what you actually traced end-to-end vs. what remains an open question. Don't pad — clean areas get one line, not a paragraph.

## Thread 1 — `imageSize`/`lazy` gating for the new gallery

**Finding 1 — 🔴 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM.** `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view-modal/bundle.jsx` (the unverified file from the brief) is one of the four base modules redirected to the Zimmermann `ProductView` override — confirmed by `product-view/index.tsx`'s own doc comment and by an exhaustive grep of every importer of `components/product-view` app-wide (exactly 4: `product-view-modal/index.jsx`, `bundle.jsx`, `bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx`, `pages/product-detail/index.jsx` — no 5th). Unlike its two siblings, `bundle.jsx` **never passes `imageSize` on either of its two `<ProductView>` calls** (parent: lines 107-124; child: lines 136-164). The parent call passes `showImageGallery={trueIfMobile}` (line 109, `trueIfMobile = useBreakpointValue({base: true, lg: false})`, line 49) — `true` below `lg`. `bundle.jsx`'s only caller, `node_modules/.../pages/cart/index.jsx:1413-1422` (bundle line-item "Edit" quick-view), also passes no `imageSize`.

**Failure scenario:** shopper on mobile/tablet opens Cart → taps "Edit" on a bundle item → `BundleProductViewModal`'s Chakra `<Modal size="4xl">` opens → the parent bundle product's gallery block now renders via the default `imageSize='md'` → `ZimmProductGallery` + a full-viewport `ZimmGalleryOverlay`, nested inside the already-open edit modal, where pre-PR it rendered the old compact `ImageGallery` (pre-PR, `'sm'` vs `'md'` was a no-op — both used the same base component). Tapping "Gallery"/"Gallery +N" pops a second full-screen dialog on top of the first. Child products in the same modal are unaffected (`showImageGallery={false}` unconditionally at line 146, so the whole gallery block — and the `imageSize` branch with it — never renders there).

This directly contradicts `product-view/index.tsx:285-291`'s own justifying comment, which claims the `'sm'`/`'md'` branch protects "the unmodified base callers that pass `imageSize=\"sm\"` (product-view-modal's quick-view **and bundle paths**, bonus-product-view-modal)". I confirmed `product-view-modal/index.jsx:44` and `bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx:466` do pass `imageSize="sm"` — the comment is correct for those two — but `bundle.jsx` passes it nowhere. The fix's own stated coverage is factually wrong about the bundle path.

Not yet verified live in a browser/mobile viewport — this is a static trace, but every code path involved is unambiguous.

**Finding 2 — PLAUSIBLE, latent, not currently live.** Confirmed via `grep -n "imageSize" overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (zero matches): all three `<ProductView>` sites (standalone ~1055, set/bundle parent ~961, per-child `.map()` loop ~987) get the new gallery. This appears **intentional, not an oversight** — the brief's specific worry that `lazy` might not be wired through does **not** hold: `product-view/index.tsx:819-823` passes `lazy={isProductPartOfSet || isProductPartOfBundle}` on both the `'sm'` and `'md'` branches (lines 815/821), and `product-detail/index.tsx:998-999` passes `isProductPartOfSet={isProductASet}` / `isProductPartOfBundle={isProductABundle}` to every child — so `lazy=true` for children, `lazy=false` for parent/standalone, matching the prop's JSDoc exactly. `ZimmMediaTile`'s `eager={i === 0 && !lazy}` (zimmProductGallery/index.tsx:206) confirms the implementation matches that contract.

What's unverified is the *consequence*: a set/bundle PDP now mounts one `ZimmProductGallery`+`ZimmGalleryOverlay` pair per product (parent + N children). Neither `product-view/index.tsx` nor `product-detail/index.tsx` has its own test file, and `zimmProductGallery`/`zimmGalleryOverlay`'s own stories/tests only exercise a single isolated instance — no "N galleries on one page" scenario anywhere. Concretely: `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:112` hardcodes `const titleId = 'zimm-gallery-overlay-title'` (not `useId()`-derived), shared identically by every instance, used for both an `id` (line 275) and `aria-labelledby` (line 133). I traced Chakra's `Modal` source (`node_modules/@chakra-ui/modal/dist/chunk-LBED2F7B.mjs:64`: `context.isOpen && jsx(Portal, ...)`) and `useZimmModal.ts:36-42` (`mounted` only ever gates SSR, is permanently `true` after first client render, and is independent of `isOpen`) — each instance's DOM subtree only exists while *that instance's own* `isOpen` is true, and each ProductView owns independent `isGalleryOverlayOpen` state, so under ordinary one-at-a-time interaction the duplicate static id never actually collides today. But nothing structurally prevents two from being open at once — it's incidental, not enforced.

## Thread 2 — ZimmColourSwatch/Group circle vs. square

**Clean.** `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` full diff: the square branch is pixel-identical to the pre-PR unconditional style object (`47px`/`72px`, `borderBottom` selected/unselected, `&:focus-visible`, `image.*` all unchanged) — only a comment moved/reworded.

**Clean, one nit.** `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts` full diff: `root.maxWidth` (`SQUARE_RESERVED_WIDTH`) and `swatches.width`/`minWidth` logic are textually identical calcs to before; `label`/`labelName`/`pagination`/`pageButton` untouched. 🔵 One-off, cosmetic: `swatches.gap` changed from literal `0` (number) to `SQUARE_GAP = '0'` (string) for the square path — Chakra's space-scale lookup coerces numeric keys to string internally, so this resolves identically; not a real regression, just worth a passing mention.

**Clean — exhaustive caller check.** `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`: only `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:218-224` passes `variant="circle"` (new); `product-detail/index.tsx:1084-1089` and the component's own `index.test.tsx` omit it (→ `'square'`, unchanged). `ZimmColourSwatch` (atom) has no external caller anywhere in the app — only rendered internally by `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` (forwards `variant={variant}`, confirmed in the diff) and its own square-only test file. No caller silently changed variant. Storybook covers circle via `CircleVariant`/`CircleVariantPaginated` (with `play` pagination assertions); Vitest coverage for circle is absent in `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx` itself (minor gap, not a defect).

**Confirmed correct default.** Both `.tsx` diffs add `variant = 'square'` as the destructed default; since the prop didn't exist pre-PR, omitting it today is provably identical to pre-PR behavior (per the pixel-identical css diff above).

**Red herring, worth flagging explicitly.** The brief's "confirmed entry point" `product-view/index.tsx:991` (`variant={id === 'color' ? 'circle' : 'square'}`) is **not part of this PR's diff and unrelated to `ZimmColourSwatch`**. Confirmed: (a) byte-identical in unmodified `node_modules/.../product-view/index.jsx:720`; (b) byte-identical in the pre-PR base worktree override at line 852; (c) it targets the **base SFCC `Swatch`** (`swatch-group/swatch`, imported at product-view/index.tsx:89), which has its own pre-existing `variant: PropTypes.oneOf(['square','circle'])` (`swatch.jsx:33/35/98`) feeding the un-overridden base `SwatchGroup` theme recipe — confirmed unrelated per `overrideStyling.md`'s own note that swatch-group has no Zimmermann override. It only executes when `renderVariationAttribute` returns `undefined` (product-view/index.tsx:953-954), which is the case for the set/bundle parent/child calls (neither supplies it) but not the standalone PDP (which short-circuits to `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`). Recommend the lead not chase this line further under Thread 2.

## What I tried to falsify
Searched for a 5th caller of overridden `ProductView` (none, exhaustive grep). Tried to find a pixel diff in square-variant output in either `.css.ts` (none). Tried to disprove the brief's "`lazy` may be unwired" hypothesis (disproved — it's wired correctly). Tried to confirm the base-Swatch `variant` line was new to this PR (disproved — pre-existing upstream and pre-PR). Traced Chakra's `Modal` source to determine whether the static `titleId` is a live or dormant bug (dormant — gated on `isOpen`). Checked `bundle.jsx`'s only caller (`cart/index.jsx`) for a smuggled `imageSize` via props-spread (none).

## What I could not verify
Did not visually/live-verify Finding 1 (bundle-edit-modal-on-mobile) or Finding 2 (N+1 galleries) in a running browser — both are static-trace-confirmed with unambiguous code paths, but not watched pixel-for-pixel. Did not audit whether the base `Swatch`/`SwatchGroup` circle rendering (the red-herring line) is itself visually correct — out of scope, pre-existing. Did not extend the "provably pixel-identical" diff technique to `zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts` (entirely new file, no square/circle distinction of its own, out of Thread 2's stated scope). Did not run Vitest/Storybook myself — "no test covers X" claims are from static reads of test file contents per the pre-measured-clean gate numbers.
